summary: A CNN analysis found Navy Federal Credit Union approved far fewer Black mortgage applicants than White applicants, even when income and other factors were similar. Lawmakers asked regulators to review its lending.
technical_summary: Navy Federal's mortgage approvals, reportedly supported by automated underwriting, showed the widest racial approval gap among major lenders. A statistical analysis found Black applicants were over twice as likely to be denied after controlling for income, debt-to-income ratio and other variables. The role of the algorithm itself is not established in the excerpts.

notes: Based on outcome disparities and allegations; the excerpts do not show how much the automated system caused them.

summary: After a game update, computer-controlled opponents in the video game Elite: Dangerous began creating extremely powerful weapons and attacking players. The developer removed the weapons and patched the problem.
technical_summary: The 2.1 update improved NPC combat AI and gave it crafting access. A networking issue let the AI merge weapon stats and abilities, producing overpowered hybrid weapons never intended by designers. The developer removed the weapons and patched the AI behavior.

summary: A 24-year-old worker at a car parts factory in India was killed by a welding robot when he reached behind it to adjust a metal sheet. Police booked the company management and contractor on negligence charges.
technical_summary: A pre-programmed industrial welding robot lifted and welded metal sheets. When a sheet became dislodged, the worker reached behind the machine and was pierced by its welding sticks. Unions alleged inadequate safety measures; the exact cause of death was reported inconsistently.

summary: A Florida sheriff's office used a data-driven policing program that flagged young people, partly from school and justice records, and then repeatedly visited their homes. Critics and a lawsuit describe it as harassment of children and families.
technical_summary: Pasco County's Intelligence-Led Policing used a point-based rubric built from school grades, absences, prior police contacts and victim records, some shared by schools and agencies, to label youths as likely future offenders. Targeted households then received repeated deputy visits, creating a self-reinforcing enforcement loop.

summary: California's COVID-19 vaccine allocation algorithm used ZIP codes instead of smaller census tracts, which an advocacy group's analysis said could leave millions of residents in the neediest neighborhoods without extra vaccine supply.
technical_summary: A vaccine-distribution algorithm built by Blue Shield allocated supply by ZIP code rather than by census tract, the unit on which the Healthy Places Index equity scores are based. The coarser geography could misdirect extra doses away from the most disadvantaged communities.
